obligation.description: With ReadOnlySafe, a caller using a fresh request context and a matching returned ReadState, and waiting until local application is strictly beyond its index, must not complete a read that omits a write completed before that read invocation when there is no intervening overwriting write. This remains required when a voter is legally demoted to a learner with StepDownOnRemoval disabled.

scope.description: Linearizable single-register read from a retained learner after legal joint demotion of its prior leader, with StepDownOnRemoval=false. A new singleton voter has completed a write before read admission; network delays can make the learner unaware of the new term until after the local ReadState is returned.
assumptions: Fresh unique ReadIndex context and matching returned context.
Caller applies entries in log order, processes Ready persistence before messages, and consumes the read only with applied>ReadState.Index.
One completed register write and no later overwriting write.
CFT network may delay/drop genuine messages without forging, editing or dropping local completion responses.
excluded: Caller serving before the documented application boundary.
StepDownOnRemoval=true as a formal scenario; it is a diagnostic control.

grounding.derivation: ReadOnlySafe promises linearizability; Node.ReadIndex/Ready specify a returned matching-context barrier and the local application threshold. A completed read after a completed write must include that write if no later write changes it. The construction honors the stricter literal applied>index wording. The demoted replica remains a learner, not a stopped removed member. StepDownOnRemoval is optional and its false setting has no documented reduction of ReadOnlySafe. Ready says SoftState need not be consumed, so adding caller-side term invalidation would introduce an extra duty absent from the supplied API.
grounding.applicability: The learner receives its barrier locally before learning the higher term, then finishes application of a real prefix beyond the barrier while the newer completed write is still undelivered.
alternatives: StepDownOnRemoval=true prevents this source path in the diagnostic control.
Greater applied index alone does not fix a barrier already below a write completed before the read invocation.
